checks.reason: Definitions4.2/4.6/5.6 define the intrinsic facet boundary and expressly allow W larger than the face span. The singleton arrangement meets (B1)-(B2), and the positive chart approach proves the [e1]x[1:1] point belongs to the strict facet boundary on E but is absent from the displayed RHS. The Lemma4.7 pointedness replacement is valid by the face property. Section5.6 explicitly uses Proposition5.10 for face maps; Remark10.8 and the wheel example require larger centers. This supports structural Major without claiming false cohomology injections.

The actually viewed publisher image at PDF111 confirms (A.25) is M^T M; extraction reordered the superscript but no report correction is needed. DefinitionsA.19-A.20 specify nonzero row-space components, not invertibility. The complex point [i:1:0] has two nonzero rows, zero Gram coordinates and two distinct projective approach limits, away from the sole source blow-up center. The real row-nonzero singular matrix separately violates (A.31). The proof on PDF112-113 uses these morphisms to construct A.16. The report correctly preserves invertible-real X(P) as counterevidence and leaves restricted construction/gluing unproved.

The publisher image at PDF112 identifies E_Fprime with a product of iterated blow-ups before removing only strict Det, so the report does not confuse an explicitly open stratum with a closed one. The two-step chart follows from first dividing all rank-one-center normal coordinates by z and then the remaining q13/z,q23/z,q33/z by w; its strict determinant is nonzero at the double exceptional corner. The canonical blow-down sends the normal restriction to diag(1,0), contradicting the stated unblown determinant-complement product. Open strata remove the extra exceptional divisors; this is the correct limited repair. A.2 and A.6.1 use the incompatible closed-locus description.

Definition5.13 minimizes among members with the same face intersection. Distinct coordinate subspaces of the standard simplex have distinct face intersections. The K4 two-edge path gives a maximal coordinate center with no nonempty core zero-edge subset, hence not an extraneous modification near that face. Proposition5.2(ii), already stated for arrangement inclusion, supplies the needed comparison; the false footnote is an unnecessary justification.

The proof on PDF55 literally equates the ambient kernel of the scalar functional with forms annihilating v. The indefinite rank-two example disproves that equality. On the positive-semidefinite polyhedron, Q=B^T B gives the necessary restricted equality; intersecting nonnegative-functional zero faces proves the original lemma. The local repair and Minor scope are correct.
